meta.title: Riverton’s street trees
meta.description: Riverton is losing its shade faster than it plants it, and 1,500 trees a year wins it back by 2040.

narrative.reasoning: A council is persuaded by a problem it can see and an answer it can fund.

brief.topic: Riverton's street trees: we are losing shade faster than we plant it

outline.bigIdea: Riverton is losing its shade faster than it plants it, and 1,500 trees a year wins it back by 2040.

beats.name: Problem: Define core challenge and stakes
beats.claim: Riverton has lost a fifth of its shade in ten years.

beats.name: Impact: Quantify cost of inaction
beats.claim: Losing shade costs the hottest neighborhoods most: Eastside runs 9°F hotter.

beats.name: Existing Approaches: Why they fall short
beats.claim: Planting 450 trees a year cannot keep up with 760 removals.

beats.name: Solution: Introduce your answer
beats.claim: Plant 1,500 trees a year for five years, Eastside and Millbrook first.

beats.name: Proof: Case studies, data, demos
beats.claim: Trees already return $6.2 million a year, more than the $2.1 million plan costs.

beats.name: Call to Action: Next steps
beats.claim: Fund the plan in the 2027 budget.

beats.notes: Councillors, the numbers here come from the division's own count. Every street in Riverton was walked for this assessment. The trees we lose are the big ones, the oaks and maples that shade a whole block. A sapling planted this spring takes most of a generation to shade that block. Eastside residents feel this every July, when the pavement holds the heat into the night. Watering is what keeps a young tree alive through its first summers. This is the part of the budget that pays for itself in stormwater and cooler streets. Councillors, the numbers here come from the division's own count.
